messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 42 omitted, sha256 6cd0c1665fefd68f>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Entailment
confidence: 70
reason: Section 3d requires a party disclosing under a legal or government demand to give the other prior notice when possible, which largely matches the hypothesis, though the notice duty is qualified by 'when possible' and the terms differ.
<quote check="exact">Each of us may disclose the other's confidential information if required to comply with a court order or other government demand that has the force of law.</quote>
<quote check="exact">when possible, give the other enough prior notice to provide a reasonable chance to seek a protective order.</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Entailment
confidence: 80
reason: Clause 3d permits legally compelled disclosure and requires each party, when possible, to give the other prior notice, which largely matches the hypothesis despite the 'when possible' qualifier.
<quote check="exact">Each of us may disclose the other's confidential information if required to comply with a court order or other government demand that has the force of law.</quote>
<quote check="exact">when possible, give the other enough prior notice to provide a reasonable chance to seek a protective order</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Entailment
confidence: 85
reason: Section 3.d requires a party compelled by court order or government demand to give the other party prior notice, where possible, before disclosing its confidential information.
<quote check="exact">Before doing so, each of us must seek the highest level of protection available and, when possible, give the other enough prior notice to provide a reasonable chance to seek a protective order.</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Entailment", "confidence": 85, "quotes": ["Each of us may disclose the other's confidential information if required to comply with a court order or other government demand that has the force of law.", "when possible, give the other enough prior notice to provide a reasonable chance to seek a protective order."], "reason": "Section 3d requires a party compelled by court order or government demand to give the other prior notice when possible before disclosing confidential information."}
